name: Columbus Museum of Art
funding: Columbus Foundation funds give ongoing support; JPMorgan Chase backs its Center for Creativity; the Pizzuti family gave its Park Street building in 2018. No donor list was found.
watch: An archive profile says Les Wexner paid for a site study and would give if the museum improved its planning. No gift is documented.
records_note: Its About page links a FY25 impact report and a Form 990 copy, names 18 trustees and shows funder logos undated.

name: Compton Verney
funding: £5.07M income (FY to Mar 2026); Compton Verney Fund endowment, Arts Council NPO, members; local firms Silson, SE-Solicitors, Goldcrest.
watch: Founded 1993 by the Peter Moores Foundation (Littlewoods pools and retail fortune); its historic endowment could be read as founding gambling money.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts 2023 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; corporate sponsors show as logos; trustees are listed with biographies.

name: Confederation Centre of the Arts
funding: C$20.7M revenue 2023-24 (C$15.1M public grants incl. C$8.6M capital), C$402k sponsorship; Sobey foundations, Cavendish Farms, CN, TD, BMO, RBC, Pepsico, Maritime Electric.
watch: Cavendish Farms (J.D. Irving; sister firm Irving Shipbuilding builds navy destroyers) sponsors; Aug 2025 John A. Macdonald fundraising campaign criticised.
records_note: Posts a 2023-24 report with named donors, sponsors, governors and condensed accounts; the full audited statements are stated to be on its website.

name: Contemporary Art Platform (CAP)
funding: Private non-profit founded 2011 by Amer Al-Huneidi; shows co-hosted with the Lebanese Business Council, Tanmia charity and UNHCR (2024)
watch: One of Kuwait's largest independent exhibition spaces, in the Shuwaikh Industrial design district, with a public art-book library.
records_note: CAP Kuwait publishes no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; its about page calls it a non-profit private organization.

name: Contemporary Image Collective
funding: No funder list is published. The Arab Fund for Arts and Culture lists a 2024 CiC project under Egypt's National Cultural Opportunities Fund. Cairo artists depend on foreign grants.
records_note: Its website fails certificate checks and could not be opened. A 2022 archived homepage shows only labs, a library and contact details.

name: Copenhagen Contemporary
funding: Culture Ministry, City of Copenhagen, Statens Kunstfond and 15 foundations in 2026, including Augustinusfonden, Det Obelske Familiefond, A.P. Møller, Ny Carlsberg, Nordea and Spar Nord.
watch: Augustinus Fonden's investment company holds over 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group; Det Obelske Familiefond's C.W. Obel A/S holds over 10% (May 2025).
records_note: It posts annual reports with accounts for 2022 to 2024, names its five board members and lists 22 supporters for 2026.

name: Corning Museum of Glass
funding: 2023: US$42.5M revenue, US$25.1M of it contributions; founder Corning Incorporated is the main funder.
watch: Founded 1951 by Corning Glass Works; budget is large but attendance (about 400k, 2012) is under the 500k line.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports from 2010 to 2024, audited statements, a named Business Alliance list and its trustees.

name: Cove Park
funding: Income was GBP 611k in FY2025 (OSCR); funders are Creative Scotland multi-year funding plus GBP 286k Culture Collective money (2026), trusts and individuals.
watch: Rural residency on Loch Long, founded in 1999 by Eileen and Peter Jacobs. Creative Scotland has funded it regularly since 2018.
records_note: Cove Park names its funders (dated 2 April 2026) and trustees and files full accounts at Companies House, but posts no annual reports.

name: Crac Occitanie
funding: Run directly by Région Occitanie with the State (Ministry of Culture, DRAC Occitanie). Sète city, Sète Agglopôle and Hérault department are partners.
records_note: Run by Région Occitanie, which posts budgets 2020 to 2026 and names 158 elected councillors; the Crac itself lists only public partners, undated.

name: CRAC Valparaíso (Centro de Residencias de Arte Contemporáneo)
funding: Fondo Nacional de Desarrollo Cultural y las Artes (FONDART), international research fellowships; non-profit research collective.
watch: Independent urban research platform in the hills of Valparaíso, running education projects on the right to the city.

name: Craft Contemporary
funding: Expenses $1.9M (FY2025); Getty, Luce, Parsons foundations, LA city and county arts funds, First Citizens Bank, Sony Pictures, members.
records_note: No annual reports found; the FY2025 Form 990 is on its site, an Annual Donor Recognition list for 2025-26 names funders, and trustees are listed.
